examples.name: Buyk
examples.proof: Buyk Corp. filed for bankruptcy and will permanently shut down after fallout from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine restricted the startup’s access to funding

examples.name: GoLemon
examples.proof: GoLemon has shut down two years after launch, citing fundraising difficulties.

risks.warning_sign: Your monthly burn rate consistently exceeds incoming revenue by more than thirty percent for two straight quarters.

examples.name: TinyOwl
examples.proof: High logistics costs and intense market competition.

examples.name: Sprig
examples.proof: The overwhelming complexity of owning meal production through delivery at scale.

risks.warning_sign: Your delivery cost per order creeps higher than the delivery fee and commission margin combined.

examples.name: Thrive
examples.proof: Food delivery startup Thrive is shutting down the operations of its consumer app after four years amid intense competition from well-funded startups in the food tech space.

risks.warning_sign: Well-funded rival apps start offering aggressive promotions and free delivery in your exact operational neighborhoods.

pattern.shut_down: The ones that shut down failed due to unsustainable unit economics, overwhelming operational complexity, and sudden capital droughts.
pattern.running: The ones still running survived through massive scale, strong venture backing, and quick adaptation to market pressures.

checklist.question: Do you have 12+ months of cash runway without securing new funding?
checklist.flag: If not, you may run out of money like Buyk and GoLemon did.

checklist.question: Can you profitably fulfill every single delivery order today?
checklist.flag: If not, you may lose money on every order like Snacc did.

checklist.question: Are your logistics costs staying below 20 percent of your average order value?
checklist.flag: If not, your operations may become too hard or costly like TinyOwl and Sprig were.

checklist.question: Do you have a clear feature or pricing advantage against well-funded giants?
checklist.flag: If not, you may be beaten by bigger competitors like Thrive was.

parts.name: Shut down in this business type
How fast they died
parts.detail: typically after about 2 years (6 with known dates)

parts.name: Recent shut-downs
parts.detail: 3 of 10 closed in the last 3 years

parts.name: Cash it took
parts.detail: shut-down companies had raised about $20M (middle value, 4 known)

companies.name: Thrive
companies.what_they_did: A Mumbai-based food delivery and restaurant tech platform that operated a consumer app and directed ONDC and marketing suite segments.
companies.story: Thrive operated for four years and secured backing from Coca Cola and Jubilant FoodWorks. Facing intense competition from well-funded giants in the food tech space and widening net losses, it decided to shut down operations of its consumer app.
reasons: Intense competition from well-funded giants in the food tech space.
Widening net losses and challenging marketplace dynamics.
companies.one_line: Intense competition from well-funded food-tech giants.

causes.proof: Food delivery startup Thrive is shutting down the operations of its consumer app after four years amid intense competition from well-funded startups in the food tech space.

companies.founder_words: The reality is that the current marketplace remains dominated by a few well-funded giants, making it extraordinarily challenging for smaller, mission-driven platforms like ours to flourish at the scale restaurants deserve

companies.name: ShopeeFood
companies.what_they_did: Offered food delivery services in Southeast Asia as part of Sea Group. Surpassed competitors in market standing.
companies.story: ShopeeFood operated as a prominent food delivery player in Southeast Asia, competing with other regional platforms. Recent market reports highlighted that ShopeeFood surpassed Gojek in market performance.
reasons: Outperformed regional competitors to secure a stronger market position.
companies.one_line: Surpassed Gojek in the growing Southeast Asian food delivery market.

companies.name: Gorillas
companies.what_they_did: It operated as a prominent ultra-fast grocery delivery startup. It faced intense capital burn within a challenging economic category.
companies.story: Gorillas scaled aggressively as part of the ultra-fast delivery wave across Europe and international markets. Although the category has destroyed billions in capital and seen many failures, Gorillas remains referenced among the major category players.
reasons: Navigated a high-attrition category characterized by immense capital destruction.
Maintained market presence despite industry-wide startup failures.
companies.one_line: Survived in a high-attrition category despite widespread industry failures.

companies.name: Jumia Food
companies.what_they_did:
Delivered food from restaurants to urban consumers.
Exited the Nigerian food delivery market.
companies.story: Jumia Food operated as an established food delivery player in Nigeria. Facing difficult market economics, the company eventually exited the country's food delivery business.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: Gojek
companies.what_they_did: Delivered food and on-demand services across Southeast Asia. Competed with other regional delivery platforms.
companies.story: Gojek established itself as a major on-demand and food delivery provider in Southeast Asia. Although ShopeeFood recently surpassed it in market metrics, Gojek continues its operations across the region.
reasons: Retained a foundational presence in the regional delivery ecosystem.
companies.one_line: Maintained ongoing food delivery operations despite competitive pressure from ShopeeFood.

companies.name: Uber Eats
companies.what_they_did: It operates a widespread online food delivery platform connecting consumers with local restaurants. It competes globally as one of the largest delivery services.
companies.story: Uber Eats established itself as a primary incumbent in the global food delivery sector alongside major competitors like DoorDash. It continues to operate at scale, navigating structural fee pressures and delivery market demands.
reasons: Maintained massive scale as a leading market incumbent.
Leveraged a widespread parent network to capture consumer order volume.
companies.one_line: Leveraged massive scale and market dominance as a primary delivery incumbent.

companies.name: Maple
companies.what_they_did: A New York City startup that built a delivery-only restaurant inside an app. It owned the entire food cycle from sourcing and preparing to delivering.
companies.story: Maple started with a pitch of providing fixed-price meals with fees included, raising around $50 million in venture capital. After struggling to keep costs in check and losing money on average orders, it ceased operations in New York and teamed up with Deliveroo.
reasons: Struggled to keep costs in check and maintain affordable prices.
Lost money on average orders making the original model unsustainable.
companies.one_line: Struggled to keep costs in check and maintain a sustainable delivery model.
companies.founder_words: Given the overlap in our goals and the significant scale of Deliveroo’s operations, working together makes sense.

companies.name: Swish
companies.what_they_did: Operated a fast-delivery food startup in India. Raised a series A funding round.
companies.story: Swish is a Bengaluru-based food delivery startup that has been operating in the Indian market. The company recently raised approximately 121.8 crore rupees in a series A funding round. Investor interest remains intact as it continues its operations.
reasons: Maintained strong operations backed by new funding rounds.
companies.one_line: Secured series A funding to continue scaling its food delivery operations.

companies.name: Ele.me
companies.what_they_did: Operated as Alibaba's food delivery branch. Appointed new executive leadership to manage its logistics.
companies.story: Ele.me developed into a major food delivery branch under Alibaba. The company underwent executive changes, naming Wu Zeming as CEO while former CEO Han Liu transitioned to lead the Instant Logistics Center.
reasons: Restructured executive leadership to support continuous logistics and delivery operations.
companies.one_line: Continued operations under Alibaba with newly appointed executive leadership.

companies.name: Rappi
companies.what_they_did: It operates a multi-service consumer tech marketplace connecting users with prepared foods, groceries, and other goods fulfilled by contractors. It acts as an everything store across Latin America.
companies.story: Backed by top venture capitalists including Sequoia and Y Combinator, Rappi grew aggressively across Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. It positioned itself as a mega high-growth platform combining features of food delivery and instant commerce.
reasons: Secured backing from top global venture capital firms.
Expanded aggressively across multiple Latin American countries as a multi-category marketplace.
companies.one_line: Aggressive multi-market expansion backed by top global venture capitalists.

companies.name: Amazon Food
companies.what_they_did: Tested a pilot food delivery service on the Amazon platform in Bengaluru. Enabled customers to order prepared meals alongside essentials.
companies.story: Amazon launched its food delivery pilot called Amazon Food in Bengaluru in May 2020. After expanding across the city and onboarding thousands of restaurant partners, the company decided to discontinue the service in December 2022 as part of an annual review and broader restructuring.
reasons: Discontinued as part of the company's annual operating planning review process
Part of broader restructuring and cost-saving measures amidst an uncertain macroeconomic environment
companies.one_line: Discontinued during an annual operating and cost-cutting review.

causes.proof: As part of our annual operating planning review process, we have made the decision to discontinue Amazon Food, our pilot food delivery business in Bengaluru

companies.name: Snacc
companies.what_they_did:
Operated as a standalone app for 10-15 minute food delivery.
Used centrally stocked hubs for quick snack and meal delivery.
companies.story: Snacc was launched in January 2025 by Swiggy as a standalone app for ultra-fast food delivery. Operating in limited markets like Bengaluru and Gurugram, it struggled to make orders profitable and was shut down in February 2026.
reasons: Struggled to make orders profitable.
Broader economics made it challenging to scale.
companies.one_line: Struggled to make orders profitable

causes.proof: as the company struggled to make orders profitable

companies.founder_words: The moment we decided to do something of our own, as a pilot called Snacc, it took us 16 days to put the application out there

companies.name: Tinmen
companies.what_they_did: Backed by Zomato, this food tech startup provided food delivery services. Shut down its entire operations.
companies.story: Tinmen launched as a Zomato-backed food tech startup focused on food delivery. It grew with backing from industry players. However, it was ultimately forced to shut down shop and cease all operations.
reasons: Closed down its food tech operations entirely
Failed to sustain its delivery model despite backing
companies.one_line: Shut down operations despite backing from major industry players.

companies.name: TinyOwl
companies.what_they_did: An Indian restaurant delivery service that operated an app across multiple cities. It stopped service in all cities except for Mumbai amid operational hurdles.
companies.story: TinyOwl raised over $27 million from marquee investors and expanded into eleven large Indian cities. Despite support, it faced high logistics costs, an oversaturated market, and mass layoffs that eventually resulted in shutting down services everywhere except Mumbai, along with plans for a merger.
reasons: High cost of logistics and an oversaturated market.
Operational troubles and mass layoffs.
companies.one_line: High logistics costs and intense market competition.

causes.proof: Issues include the high cost of logistics and a oversaturated market

companies.name: SpoonRocket
companies.what_they_did: An on-demand food delivery service operating in the United States. It cooked and delivered meals to consumers.
companies.story: SpoonRocket entered the on-demand food delivery market to provide quick meal deliveries. However, due to the tough economics of the business, it shut down its operations in the U.S.
reasons: Tough economics of the on-demand food business model.
companies.one_line: Shut down due to the extreme difficulty of the on-demand food business model.

companies.name: Grab
companies.what_they_did: Provided food delivery services across Southeast Asia. Led the regional market as GMV grew.
companies.story: Grab expanded its presence across Southeast Asia to capture a major share of the digital delivery market. Recent reports indicate that the region's food delivery GMV hit $19.3 billion with Grab leading the market.
reasons: Maintained market leadership amidst regional growth in Southeast Asia.
companies.one_line: Led the Southeast Asian food delivery market as regional GMV expanded.

companies.name: Zero Grocery
companies.what_they_did: It operated as an online grocery delivery startup based in northern California. It expanded to Los Angeles shortly before its sudden closure.
companies.story: Zero Grocery grew rapidly as a delivery startup in northern California and even expanded to Los Angeles after raising $12 million. However, it abruptly shut down shortly after, leaving local businesses and product suppliers owed money and wondering what went wrong.
reasons: Abruptly closed operations despite recent funding rounds and expansion.
Left northern California suppliers and businesses owed money.
companies.one_line: Abrupt closure following rapid expansion and funding confusion.

companies.name: Deliveroo
companies.what_they_did: A heavily funded European food-delivery startup operating across multiple countries and cities globally. It integrates technology platforms to help restaurants launch and take menus nationwide.
companies.story: Deliveroo grew from a local London affair into a global business operating across multiple countries and cities. It absorbed team members and technology from shutting down platforms like Maple and was later acquired by DoorDash.
reasons: Achieved massive international scale and strategic acquisitions.
companies.one_line: Acquired by DoorDash after scaling into a global delivery network.
companies.founder_words: In our mission to build the very best food delivery service in the world, this is another big step as we deliver more top quality food to more customers around the world.

companies.name: Grubhub
companies.what_they_did: Operated a US food delivery firm connecting customers with restaurants. Acquired smaller projects like Collin Wallace's startup in 2011.
companies.story: Grubhub grew to become a major player in the food delivery sector, eventually acquiring early online food ordering projects. Recently, the US food delivery firm faced workforce reductions, laying off over 20% of its workforce.
reasons: Implemented workforce reductions and navigated industry cost pressures.
companies.one_line: Laid off over 20% of its workforce while maintaining ongoing delivery operations.

companies.name: Buyk
companies.what_they_did: It provided 15-minute grocery deliveries in New York City and Chicago with no minimum order or fees. Its Russian founders provided bridge financing until the next round closed.
companies.story: Buyk launched in New York City as an ultra-fast grocery delivery service backed by Russian founders. Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, sanctions restricted the company's access to funding. Consequently, it filed for bankruptcy, laid off hundreds of employees, and permanently shut down.
reasons: Sanctions due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine restricted access to funding.
Failed to secure a deal or financing after bridge funding dried up.
companies.one_line: Sanctions over Russia's invasion of Ukraine restricted funding access.

causes.proof: Buyk Corp. filed for bankruptcy and will permanently shut down after fallout from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine restricted the startup’s access to funding

companies.name: GoLemon
companies.what_they_did: A Nigerian grocery delivery startup founded by former Paystack employees. It offered on-demand grocery delivery to urban consumers.
companies.story: GoLemon launched to make grocery shopping easier for urban consumers in Nigeria. However, after two years of operation, it faced fundraising difficulties, could not find a sustainable path forward, and shut down its operations.
reasons: Inability to secure additional funding.
Difficult economics of food and grocery delivery in the region.
companies.one_line: Fundraising difficulties and tough market economics.

causes.proof: GoLemon has shut down two years after launch, citing fundraising difficulties.

companies.founder_words: It’s difficult to get started right now and get traction, but if we can weather the storm right now, I think we would have been able to build a formidable business

companies.name: Delivery.com
companies.what_they_did: It connects users with local restaurant and retail merchants for delivery across multiple states using a franchise model. It adapted its platform to offer pandemic-related relief and merchant fee waivers.
companies.story: Delivery.com built a national presence across 1,800 cities with thousands of merchant partners. During the COVID-19 pandemic, it faced severe disruptions as urban customers left cities and merchants closed, prompting the company to cut delivery fees, waive merchant percentages, and pivot engineering efforts to support relief.
reasons: Lowered delivery fees and waived merchant commission percentages during crises.
Adapted engineering teams to build relevant pandemic relief programs.
companies.one_line: Lowered merchant fees and adapted operations to survive the pandemic squeeze.

risks_handled.how: Lowered delivery fees by 10 percent and waived merchant fees entirely during the COVID-19 pandemic.

companies.name: Sprig
companies.what_they_did: A startup that made and delivered its own food, offering a daily rotating menu. It experimented with walk-in kitchen services and deliveries via Caviar.
companies.story: Sprig raised $56.7 million to cook and deliver its own meals using a self-engineered system. Despite high demand for its quality food, the complexity of owning meal production through delivery at scale led to shutting down its app.
reasons: The complexity of owning meal production through delivery at scale.
Struggled with operational challenges and market pressures in cities like Chicago.
companies.one_line: The overwhelming complexity of owning meal production through delivery at scale.

causes.proof: the complexity of owning meal production through delivery at scale was a challenge.

companies.founder_words: No question, I’m sad that the Sprig model did not work out — but the food delivery space on the whole is growing.

companies.name: Getir
companies.what_they_did: It offers instant delivery services for groceries and daily essentials. It secured massive late-stage funding rounds to fuel its market operations.
companies.story: Getir grew as a major international player in the instant delivery sector. It continued its operations by closing a massive $768 million Series E funding round, which brought its overall valuation to $11.8 billion.
reasons: Successfully secured massive funding rounds like its $768 million Series E.
Maintained high valuation and investor backing.
companies.one_line: Secured massive multi-million-dollar funding rounds to sustain operations.

companies.name: Bolt Food
companies.what_they_did:
Delivered food from restaurants to urban consumers.
Exited the Nigerian food delivery business.
companies.story: Bolt Food operated as an established player in the food delivery market. The company later exited its operations in Nigeria.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: Dazo
companies.what_they_did: Operated as an Indian food tech startup delivering meals. Shut down its operations amid a wave of food startup demises.
companies.story: Dazo started as a food tech startup operating in India's food delivery sector. It grew during an active period for food startups but faced severe market pressures. The company ultimately shut down its operations.
reasons: Faced difficulties in the early Indian food tech market
Shut down operations alongside other failing food startups
companies.one_line: Shut down operations amid early challenges in the Indian food tech sector.

companies.name: Zomato
companies.what_they_did: Delivers food from many restaurants to customers via an online platform. Competes in the food tech space and quick commerce.
companies.story: Zomato has grown to become a dominant force in the Indian food tech space. It successfully navigated the pandemic and market challenges through strategic moves. It currently maintains a market presence and expands into quick commerce and related offerings.
reasons: Maintains a small lead in the market against rival Swiggy
Managed to tide over the pandemic with strategic acquisitions and by changing business models
Expanded into quick commerce and related domains
companies.one_line: Maintains a market lead through strategic changes and expansion.

companies.name: FoodCourt
companies.what_they_did:
Operated as a food-tech platform in Nigeria.
Temporarily suspended its operations.
companies.story: FoodCourt operated as a food-tech platform in Nigeria. The company faced fundraising challenges and temporarily suspended its operations.
reasons: Faced fundraising challenges leading to temporary suspension.
companies.one_line: Fundraising challenges

causes.proof: pointing to fundraising challenges as a key factor behind its decision

companies.name: EatFresh
companies.what_they_did: Operated as a food tech startup offering meal delivery. Shut down its food delivery service to pivot.
companies.story: EatFresh started as a food tech startup delivering meals to consumers. Facing the challenges of standard food delivery, it decided to discontinue its core food delivery service. The company subsequently shifted focus to cater bulk orders.
reasons: Discontinued its standard food delivery service
Pivoted away from delivery to cater bulk orders instead
companies.one_line: Shut down its food delivery service to focus on bulk orders.

companies.name: TastyKhana.in
companies.what_they_did: TastyKhana.in served as one of the first online food ordering portals in India. It allowed customers to order food online.
companies.story: TastyKhana.in started as one of the first online food ordering portals in India. It eventually grew its presence and was later acquired, becoming a FoodPanda company.
reasons: It was acquired by another company.
companies.one_line: It was acquired to become a FoodPanda company.

companies.name: Robinhood
companies.what_they_did: Provided food delivery services in Thailand. Halted shutdown plans amid external buyer interest.
companies.story: Robinhood operated a food delivery service in Thailand's competitive sector. Although it faced potential closure, SCB X halted the planned shutdown of Robinhood due to emerging buyer interest.
reasons: Halted shutdown operations after attracting potential acquisition interest from buyers.
companies.one_line: Suspended shutdown plans due to active buyer interest.

companies.name: Swiggy
companies.what_they_did: Operates an app-based food delivery service connecting users to restaurants. Backed by major institutional investors.
companies.story: Swiggy is a major player in the food tech industry backed by prominent investors like SoftBank, Prosus Ventures, and Invesco. It competes closely with Zomato and has evolved through market shifts and changing business models.
reasons: Backed by strong institutional investors like SoftBank, Prosus Ventures and Invesco
Adapted business models to navigate pandemic and market challenges
Expanded into new verticals like live events and quick commerce
companies.one_line: Kept alive through strong venture backing and business model adaptation.

companies.name: Munchery
companies.what_they_did: An on-demand prepared food delivery service that cooked and delivered meals. It faced a rough time with financial struggles and food waste.
companies.story: Munchery operated in the on-demand food delivery space and experienced a rough period marked by layoffs, burning through capital, and food waste. It ultimately joined the list of failed food delivery startups.
reasons: Burned through most of the money it had raised.
Faced severe operational difficulties like layoffs and food waste.
companies.one_line: Burned through raised capital amidst severe operational difficulties.

causes.proof: between the layoffs, burning through most of the money it has raised and food waste.

companies.name: DoorDash
companies.what_they_did: It operates a major food and grocery delivery platform and recently launched ultra-fast delivery services in cities like New York. It also acquired Deliveroo for $3.86 billion.
companies.story: DoorDash expanded rapidly as a dominant food delivery platform in the United States and globally. It recently announced a deal to acquire Deliveroo for $3.86 billion, bringing its combined user base to 50 million active users across more than 40 countries.
reasons: Expanded globally and made strategic acquisitions like Deliveroo to scale its presence.
Continuously launched new service lines like ultra-fast delivery.
companies.one_line: Strategic global expansion and major acquisitions like Deliveroo.
